transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-08 15:00 PDT | Duration: 54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Li (Redwood CSM), Irene Morales (SableGrid VP Eng), Tomás Rivera (SRE), Elena Park (Head ML), Samir Gupta (Security)

Topics: RCA recap, technical deep dive on KV cache / eviction, rollout & canary strategy, compliance/KMS questions, runbook and drill scheduling, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Maya Chen: alright everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight — follow up from last week's bridgecall, go over the RCA summary, and nail down the action items. hi, Irene, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Irene Morales: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate the recap — we had a rough week, so want to be sure this doesn't repeat.
[00:20] Ravi Patel: quick intro, I'm Ravi, did the trace analysis and replay on Redwood's end. I want to walk through what we found and then we can discuss mitigations.
[00:30] Tomás Rivera: just FYI I'm on from the SRE side — I'll call out the prod constraints and the traffic patterns we saw.
[00:35] Elena Park: and I'm focused on the model rollout piece — the quantized variant we used, and how it may have affected KV semantics.
[00:45] Maya Chen: ok Ravi, take it away.

[01:00] Ravi Patel: so short version: incident triggered by an operational rollout of a q4-bit quantized variant of the v2-chat model. After the rollout we saw a small fraction of requests start to experience very high token generation latencies and intermittent partial responses. On inspecting traces we saw that a subset of workers were evicting KV prefixes prematurely which caused re-warm of KV and long tail latency for those requests. This combined with aggressive continuous batching caused request accumulation on the hot path.
[01:30] Ravi Patel: the KV misbehavior looked like a checksum mismatch between the persisted prefix index and in-memory offsets after serialization across filesystem snapshotting during a nightly maintenance window. it was rare but once it happened, the eviction loop didn't backoff properly.
[01:50] Elena Park: to add, the quantized runtime changed the memory layout slightly which affected the serialized offsets across the worker. We should've validated cross-version serialization invariants during the rollout.
[02:10] Tomás Rivera: in our metrics the onset was a 12 minute window where p95 token latency doubled and error rate rose from 0.1% to 2.3%. CPU on the affected hosts spiked as well.
[02:28] Irene Morales: quick question — is this purely a Redwood runtime issue, or did our config change (we bumped max-concurrency last week)?
[02:38] Ravi Patel: short answer: it's an interaction. The config bump exposed the bad path faster; with the previous concurrency the mis-serialization would have still existed but probably not reached the threshold to cascade.
[02:50] Maya Chen: and just to be clear, we saw graceful degradation on many routes but for the critical route (document summarization) you saw partial outputs and timeouts.
[03:00] Tomás Rivera: yes exactly. we had partial completions and the application layer retried which amplified the queue.

[03:15] Speaker 1 (Noah?): can you explain "KV prefix" in plain english for the execs?
[03:20] Ravi Patel: sure — think of KV cache as the model's working memory for recent tokens. prefix is the beginning portion of the conversation that's reused. if the cache evicts or is misaligned, the model has to recompute from scratch which costs time.
[03:36] Irene Morales: okay thanks.

[03:45] Ravi Patel: root causes we've classified: 1) serialization incompatibility introduced by quantized binary layout changes, 2) missing checksum validation on startup for persisted prefix shards, 3) overly aggressive eviction loop with inadequate backoff, and 4) operational config changes that increased exposure.
[04:05] Elena Park: and from model side, we missed one unit test — a cross-version load test for serialized KV. that's on us.

[04:20] Maya Chen: let's move to mitigations — what did Redwood do immediately and what's recommended?

[04:30] Ravi Patel: immediate mitigation we rolled out: 1) revert to the last stable model variant for affected services, 2) applied a hotfix to the eviction loop that enforces exponential backoff on mismatch detection, 3) enabled a temporary prefix checksum guard to detect and refuse loads with mismatched checksums rather than silently proceeding. That reduced incidences in our internal replay.
[05:00] Ravi Patel: recommended near-term: run a full replay at your traffic scale to validate eviction behavior; patch the serialization invariants in the quantized runtime; introduce a canary policy where only 2% of traffic hits the new variant for 24 hours with KV consistency checks; adjust autoscale triggers to allow buffer capacity during rollouts.
[05:28] Tomás Rivera: about autoscale — we saw scaling lag because our horizontal scaling policy had a high cooldown. we need tighter scale-up for token generation spikes.
[05:40] Maya Chen: for SableGrid we propose a tailored canary + preflight checks plan — Redwood will provide a canary policy template and a preflight checklist.

[05:55] Irene Morales: what about the audit/compliance side? our security team needs traceability for any state that affects PII-handling flows.
[06:05] Samir Gupta: yes we need logs that show KV-checksum passes, KMS key-id, and an immutable audit trail for model rollouts. any quick wins?
[06:15] Ravi Patel: we can add a log line on startup that includes the model version, serialization checksum, and the KMS key fingerprint used for any encrypted checkpoints. Redwood's private deployment supports forwarding these logs to your SIEM. we'll link the schema.
[06:34] Samir Gupta: ok we'll want that in writing.

[06:45] Elena Park: also curious about fallback model variants — if the primary has trouble, can Redwood route to a smaller quantized variant automatically?
[06:55] Ravi Patel: yes routing policy supports automatic fallback to a pinned safe model variant. tradeoff is that smaller variants increase latency for some prompts, but it's a predictable behavior. We can set policy to prefer latency SLOs or cost.

[07:12] Maya Chen: let's discuss long-term hardenings.
[07:18] Ravi Patel: long-term: 1) enforce cross-version serialization tests in CI including fuzz tests, 2) checksum + signature for persisted KV shards, 3) stronger canary orchestration in the control plane (traffic ramp with health gates), 4) better instrumentation: token-level traces for evictions, and 5) an ops runbook with playbooks for detection and mitigation.
[07:45] Irene Morales: what's involved to get the checksum/signature in our Private deployment? will it need KMS changes?
[07:53] Ravi Patel: we'll sign persisted shards with your KMS key -- Redwood supports KMS/HSM integration. We will add a flow: when writing shards, sign them; on startup verify signature. If verification fails, worker refuses to load and reports an alarm. That ties into audit logs.
[08:12] Samir Gupta: KMS rotation is important — how will rotation impact existing signatures?
[08:18] Ravi Patel: rotation policy supported: we can keep a key history and accept prior signatures for a defined transition window. We'll provide the policy docs.

[08:30] Tomás Rivera: operationally, we need mitigations that don't require full rollback of models, since that disrupts our ML pipelines. Canary + checksum sounds ok. but we need the runbook to automate the rollback threshold.
[08:46] Maya Chen: agreed. Noah, can you own the runbook drafting?
[08:50] Noah Li: yeah I'll take that — draft a 1 pager plus escalation ladder.

[09:00] Ravi Patel: for the replay that Maya mentioned, Redwood will provide a synthetic replay harness and we will run it against SableGrid's traffic sample. We need the traffic snapshot (anonymized) and the target sequences you want validated.
[09:18] Tomás Rivera: we'll export the windows and sample and share a link.

[09:25] Speaker 2 (Irene): curious about monitoring — can we get a dashboard for KV checksum failures and eviction rates?
[09:32] Ravi Patel: yes we'll add a dashboard tile in Redwood Console: eviction rate, checksum mismatch count, average rewarm time, and p50/p95 token latency for affected routes. We'll share a dashboard JSON you can import.

[09:48] Elena Park: on the model side, we'll add cross-version loading tests and push them into our CI. will Redwood run any cross-version integration tests as part of model onboarding?
[09:58] Ravi Patel: we can run a light integration test in the staging area and recommend a heavy replay in your pre-prod. For hosted variants we run the integration tests before rollout, but for Private we can run them together with your pipeline.

[10:15] Maya Chen: let's capture risk/reward — if SableGrid wants the fastest path to full confidence, what do we recommend?
[10:22] Ravi Patel: do the checksum signing + canary + replay + adjusted autoscale. That combination addresses detection (checksum), prevention (canary), validation (replay), and resilience (autoscale + fallback).

[10:35] Tomás Rivera: timeline question — how long to get the checksum gating into our private deploy?
[10:40] Ravi Patel: engineering estimate: 2 weeks for initial sign/verify flow in the private runtime and 3–4 days for docs and dashboard wiring. We'll prioritize as a patch.

[10:55] Irene Morales: cost question — if we run extended canaries or replay at full scale, what are the expected cost impacts?
[11:02] Maya Chen: we'll provide a cost projection in the follow-up packet. conservative estimate: replay at production scale for a day could be roughly one to two weeks of normal inference spend depending on sampling, but we can do sampled replays to cut cost.

[11:20] Samir Gupta: from compliance — we'll need the immutable audit entries for any rollback or model promotion decisions for the quarter. Can Redwood add a promotion/rollback event to the audit log?
[11:30] Ravi Patel: yes promotions/rollbacks are already captured; we'll ensure the payload includes the serialized checksum and KMS key id.

[11:40] Speaker 3 (Tomás): ok, can we walk through the runbook flow quickly? detection -> isolation -> fallback -> rollback -> excavation?
[11:48] Noah Li: detection: alerts on checksum mismatch or eviction rate spike. isolation: cordon node and shift traffic off. fallback: route to safe model variant. rollback: initiate model rollback if canary fails health gates. excavation: postmortem and tag for follow-up. We'll include exact thresholds.

[12:10] Ravi Patel: one nuance — automatic rollback is risky for queries under heavy stateful load; recommended approach is automated fallback for serving while rollback is a manual decision with approval steps.

[12:25] Irene Morales: that makes sense. we want predictable behavior.

[12:32] Maya Chen: ok concrete asks before the follow-up: Ravi will run the eviction replay and share logs; Maya to send RCA + benchmark; Noah to draft runbook; Samir to confirm KMS audit needs; Tomás share traffic slice.

[12:50] Elena Park: minor note — we'll add a CI gate to our model release pipeline that runs a small serialization-load test.
[12:58] Ravi Patel: perfect, that'll reduce future exposure.

[13:10] Irene Morales: timeline for next check-in? we want to reconvene after the replay and initial patch.
[13:15] Maya Chen: propose 2026-09-21 to review replay results and runbook drill schedule. does that work?
[13:22] Tomás Rivera: works for me.
[13:24] Samir Gupta: works.

[13:30] Maya Chen: ok I'll send calendar invite and include the checklist. quick note on docs — I'll attach the console dashboard JSON, the RCA slide, and a trimmed benchmark CSV.

[13:42] Ravi Patel: one more technical caveat: if you run the replay in a shared hosted environment, we recommend isolation to avoid noisy neighbors. For Private customers we can orchestrate on your infra.

[13:58] Irene Morales: we'll likely take Private orchestration for the replay. we'll confirm in the ticket.

[14:05] Speaker 4 (Elena): small question — is there any risk to user data with the eviction bug?
[14:10] Ravi Patel: no direct exfiltration risk detected. The issue is operational correctness and latency; persisted shards were internal serialized state without PII. But we'll include a confirmation in the RCA.

[14:25] Maya Chen: great. any other open items?
[14:30] (brief pause)
[14:32] Irene Morales: no, thank you for the quick turnaround.
[14:35] Maya Chen: thanks all — recap: action items (Ravi, Maya, Noah, Samir, Tomás) and follow-up on 2026-09-21. we'll include the runbook and schedule the drill.
[14:50] Tomás Rivera: thanks.
[14:52] Noah Li: thanks everyone.
[14:55] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription: slight overlaps, some speaker labels may be generic. occasional technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "q4-bit" instead of the specific quantization name).
